newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma dismisses Suu Kyi charge over murder threat.
newsitem.headline: Burma dismisses Suu Kyi charge over murder threat.

text.p: A Burmese government spokesman on Tuesday dismissed Aung San Suu Kyi's charge that an official had told supporters to kill her, saying the opposition leader had been watching too many movies.
"She's been watching too many Alfred Hitchcock suspense movies and I dont know from where she is getting all these ideas. This is quite silly," the spokesman told Reuters.
Suu Kyi said on Monday she had learned that Railway Minister Win Sein had told members of the pro-government Union Solidarity and Development Association (USDA) to kill her last November.
She said the minister had "roughly told them that I should be killed".
In November an unidentified group of men attacked Suu Kyi's motorcade near her residence with sticks and stones.
Suu Kyi was not hurt in the incident but her car was heavily damaged. She blamed the government for the attack.
The opposition National League for Democracy (NLD) has lodged a complaint with the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) over the murder threat, she said.
The SLORC said on Saturday that public access to Suu Kyi's home in central Rangoon would remain blocked until her personal safety was assured.
But Suu Kyi said she could take care of herself and that the military government's insistence on providing her security would only curb her movement and deny visitors access to her.
"People from whom they will have to protect me from are those in fact who are in authority," she said.
